newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia central bank assets show Q2 increase.
newsitem.headline: Latvia central bank assets show Q2 increase.

text.p: Latvia's central bank net foreign assets rose 15.4 percent to 283.5 million lats in the second quarter of 1996 versus the first three months and reserve money grew 19.1 percent to 311.3 million lats, it said on Tuesday.
In a second quarter report, the central bank also said that bank deposits by private persons and domestic companies rose by 7.3 percent to 314.2 million lats during the second quarter.
Bank deposits have been gradually rising as people get over a crisis in the banking sector last year.
The bank said that broad money supply rose 40 million lats during the second quarter to 544.4 million lats.
But the bank said credits granted by banks did not change much, reaching 196.4 million lats at the end of the second quarter, versus 196.5 million lats in the first three months.

Increasing confidence in the banking sector also showed up in more domestic interbank credits, which rose from 49.9 million lats in the first quarter to 124.2 million lats in the second quarter. Credits to foreign institutions were stable at just over 1.8 billion lats.
The central bank said the number of participants in the interbank market was 15 to 16 banks each month.
